key_insight: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT) treats attention keys and values as reusable memory across model depths and repeated loops. This lets the model selectively reuse earlier information rather than relying only on what adjacent loops pass forward.
problem_solved: Looped Transformers gain expressive power by repeatedly applying shared layers, but this repetition comes with efficiency costs. The paper rethinks how information moves between loops to improve that trade-off.
method: Introduce Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA), which uses attention keys and values as memory.
Selectively reuse this memory across depths and loops.
Include a loop-residual variant, MoLT-R, that retains the residual stream; further details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: MoLT offers a design direction for making shared-layer Transformers more expressive without simply adding distinct layers. The provided abstract does not include results, so practical efficiency gains remain unverified here.
visual_elements: Loop diagram showing a shared Transformer block applied repeatedly.
Memory-bank illustration showing keys and values reused across depths and loops.
Side-by-side information-flow diagrams comparing conventional loop connections with MoLA.
Conceptual expressivity–efficiency trade-off graphic, clearly labeled as illustrative rather than measured.
paper_authors: Lianghui Zhu, Shijie Wang, Xinggang Wang, Jinze Bai, Bo Wang
